behavior.arguments: rdi = the 64-bit input value. No other argument is read and no other field is written.

edges.all_ones: with input 0xffffffffffffffff the result is 64: every SWAR stage preserves the full count through the 32-bit fold.
edges.mixed: with input 0x123456789abcdef0 the result equals the input's bit count (32).
edges.single_high_bit: with input 0x8000000000000000 the result is 1: the high bit survives every mask stage and the fold.

behavior.entry_shape: Opens with mov %rdi,%rax (NOT endbr64); zero branches, zero calls inside; a single ret at offset 0x61.
behavior.return_rule: Let x = rdi. x = x - ((x >> 1) & 0x5555555555555555); x = (x & 0x3333333333333333) + ((x >> 2) & 0x3333333333333333); x = (x + (x >> 4)) & 0xf0f0f0f0f0f0f0f; then the 32-bit fold: eax = (x >> 0x20) + (x & 0xffffffff) truncated to 32 bits; ecx = eax + (eax >> 0x10) truncated to 32 bits; eax = ecx + (ecx >> 8) truncated to 32 bits; return eax & 0x7f. All 64-bit steps wrap modulo 2^64; the fold steps truncate to 32 bits, matching the 32-bit registers in the bytes.

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, without a guessed loader or Ghidra rebase. The ELF section table maps .text with file offset = VA - 0x1000; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offset and VA. The tools resolve sections rather than assuming one global VA/file-offset relationship.

incoming_pattern_scan.note: Byte-pattern scan over the full .text section (70,370,352 bytes) for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on the window start; exactly 25 sites found, each boundary-confirmed inside its caller FDE (6 distinct caller FDEs: 1 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 18 sites). This is explicitly not a complete xref census: indirect calls, tail jumps, and PLT references are out of scope for the scan.
incoming_pattern_scan.relocation_note: No R_X86_64_RELATIVE record in any .rela.* section names this window as addend (full-section scan: 80,022 .rela.dyn + 278 .rela.plt entries).

unwindless.gap_note: No FDE record covers the window. The gap between the bracketing FDEs is 124 bytes: 12 int3 + 98-byte window + 14 int3. The checker walks every .eh_frame record and proves no FDE pc/range contains 0x5660010, and no FDE record starts inside the gap [0x5660004, 0x5660080).
unwindless.next_fde_note: NEXT FDE pc 0x5660080..0x5660092 is the __cxa_atexit stub (endbr64, mov, xor, jmp to __cxa_atexit@plt).
unwindless.prev_fde_note: PREV FDE pc 0x565ff80..0x5660004 ends with the ret at 0x5660003, exactly where the leading int3 run starts.
